title: Uncommon Words from Two Sentences
summary: Define a sentence as a string of words separated by single spaces, where each word consists only of lowercase letters.
statement: Define a sentence as a string of words separated by single spaces, where each word consists only of lowercase letters. A word is considered uncommon if it appears exactly once in one of the sentences and does not appear in the other sentence. Given two sentences, s1 and s2, return a list of all such uncommon words in any order.
constraints: Return words appearing exactly once across both sentences; order is irrelevant.
hints: Uncommon means global frequency exactly one, not one occurrence per sentence.
Count the concatenated token streams once.
Return keys whose Counter value equals one.
Global counting naturally excludes repeated words within or across sentences.
editorial: Global counting naturally excludes repeated words within or across sentences.
